name: cv-baseline-v4
hypothesis: Era anchor for cv-medium-v4: frozen yamnet linear probe, 400 epochs, on medium now including Hard Negatives.
conclusion: 0.324 (0.262 incl. quiet). Anchor for v4. Not comparable to v3's 0.330: the data changed (Hard Negatives added).

name: v4-ft
hypothesis: Fine-tuning YAMNet layers 12-14 (depth12, backbone LR 1e-5, 30 epochs, linear head) beats the frozen anchor on the new data.
conclusion: +0.051 (0.375). Val sens was still rising at epoch 30, so 30 epochs may understate it. All grid runs use the same 30-epoch budget, so the grid is matched.

name: v4-ft-dense
hypothesis: A Dense(1024) ReLU head on the depth12 fine-tuned trunk beats the linear head.
conclusion: 0.376 vs v4-ft 0.375: no gain from the dense head.

name: v4-ft-ps
hypothesis: Last era's best (fine-tuned depth12 trunk + octave-up pitch-shift twin, linear head) holds up on the Hard Negatives data at 30 epochs.
conclusion: 0.452 (0.372 incl. quiet), +0.128 vs anchor and +0.077 vs v4-ft. Grid winner. Reproduces v3's 0.472/0.454. Hard folds up vs anchor: 1_95 0.07->0.20, 1_150 0.25->0.31, willard 0.39->0.58.

name: v4-ft-ps-dense
hypothesis: A Dense(1024) head on the pitch-shift fine-tuned trunk beats the linear head.
conclusion: 0.432, -0.020 vs v4-ft-ps. The dense head doesn't help; if anything it's slightly worse.

name: v4-ft-ctx
hypothesis: Temporal context (neighbouring frames through a shared depth12 tail) adds to fine-tuning.
conclusion: 0.416, +0.041 vs v4-ft but -0.036 vs v4-ft-ps. Context helps; pitch-shift helps more.

name: v4-ft-ctx-dense
hypothesis: A Dense(1024) head on the context fine-tuned trunk beats the linear head.
conclusion: 0.384, -0.032 vs v4-ft-ctx. The dense head is worse again.

name: v4-ft-psud
hypothesis: Adding an octave-DOWN third view (centre half, resampled) to v4-ft-ps's [plain, up] improves on it.
conclusion: 0.452 (0.371 incl. quiet), +0.000 vs v4-ft-ps. Adding down to up is flat. Down alone and other down methods queued (HANDOFF.md).

name: v4-ft-ps-e60
hypothesis: v4-ft-ps at 60 epochs beats 30 epochs (the epoch confirmation before moderate).
conclusion: 0.468 (0.386 incl. quiet), +0.016 vs v4-ft-ps at 30 epochs. About one delta SD (~0.014), below the ~0.027 MDE. Weak evidence 60 is no worse and may help; 60 is fine for the moderate run.

name: v4-ft-psd
hypothesis: An octave-DOWN second view alone (centre half, resampled), in place of v4-ft-ps's up view, helps over no shift.
conclusion: 0.404 (0.336 incl. quiet), -0.048 vs v4-ft-ps; +0.029 vs v4-ft (0.375), at the ~0.027 MDE. Down alone is at most a small gain; up carries the pitch-shift effect. Hard folds below ps: 1_95 0.167, willard 0.483.

name: v4-ft-pshd
hypothesis: Octave-down resampling applied to both halves (full frame coverage) beats centre-half down.
conclusion: 0.394 (0.323 incl. quiet), -0.058 vs v4-ft-ps; +0.019 vs v4-ft (0.375), noise-level. Both-halves vs centre down: -0.010, no difference. 1_150 0.361 (vs ps 0.312) is a one-fold lead only; 1_95 0.128 lowest of the grid.

name: v4-ft-vd
hypothesis: Octave-down via phase vocoder (duration kept) beats resampled down.
conclusion: 0.401 (0.331 incl. quiet), -0.051 vs v4-ft-ps; +0.026 vs v4-ft (0.375), noise-level. Vocoder vs resample down: -0.003, no difference.

name: v4-ft-vu
hypothesis: Octave-up via phase vocoder (duration kept) beats v4-ft-ps's resampled up.
conclusion: 0.455 (0.377 incl. quiet), +0.003 vs v4-ft-ps. Vocoder up equals resample up; resample stays preferred (no deployment cost measured for the vocoder). Hard folds track ps: 1_95 0.215, 1_150 0.315, willard 0.573.

name: v4-ft-vud
hypothesis: Vocoder up + down views beat a single up view.
conclusion: 0.428 (0.353 incl. quiet), -0.024 vs v4-ft-ps and -0.027 vs v4-ft-vu, at the MDE. Adding down to up does not help; weak sign it hurts with the vocoder. 1_95 0.226 is the grid high at 30 epochs (one fold).

name: v4-ft-pshud
hypothesis: Resampled up + down applied to both halves (four views) beats v4-ft-ps.
conclusion: 0.455 (0.374 incl. quiet), +0.003 vs v4-ft-ps. Flat; not worth 4 views (~2x train time). Ran without RAM kill. 1_150 0.407 is the grid high (one fold, 21 events). Grid verdict: up is the effect, method and down don't matter; v4-ft-ps stays the pick.
